Article Title: ‘Zero tolerance for violations’: FSSAI directs 5-star hotels ahead of Brics Summit
Article Text:
FSSAI held a meeting with representatives of leading five-star hotels from across the country

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued directions to major five-star hotels that there should be a “zero-tolerance” approach towards food safety and other violations ahead of the two-day Brics Summit in the national capital."FSSAI issued clear directives emphasising zero tolerance for any violations," ANI quoted sources as saying.The directions were conveyed recently at a crucial meeting convened by the food regulator with representatives of leading five-star hotels across the country, where a “zero-tolerance” approach towards violations of food safety measures was stressed ahead of the Brics Summit.“The meeting centred on evaluating current regulatory compliance, hygiene benchmarks, kitchen safety protocols and overall food safety. All major five-star properties reported strong adherence to safety norms and shared positive updates on their existing compliance frameworks,” the sources added.Ahead of the Brics Summit, the FSSAI has significantly ramped up random inspections at five-star establishments to ensure strict compliance with hygiene and food safety standards.The regulator’s move came days after it conducted inspections at two major hotels in Delhi’s Aerocity, where several deficiencies were found.FSSAI officials inspected the kitchens of JW Marriott and Hotel Andaz, where issues including foul smell, cockroaches and flies were reported. Complaints related to cockroaches, flies and foul odour were also recorded during the inspections.Several bread packets bearing expired stickers were found at the hotels. Around 87 kg of expired sweets were also discovered in the confectionery area and destroyed on the spot. In the pastry section, inspectors found expired cake bases, along with flies and cockroaches.The inspection continued for around two days, during which 59 deficiencies were recorded.The BRICS Summit will be held at the Bharat Mandapam convention centre in Delhi.
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued directions to major five-star hotels that there should be a “zero-tolerance” approach towards food safety. The directions were conveyed recently at a crucial meeting convened by the food regulator with representatives of leading hotels across the country.

Article Title: 'He can remove Pakistan from world picture': Eknath Shinde after Sharif crops PM Modi from SCO pic
Article Text:
Shinde's remarks came after Sharif’s office shared an edited version of the SCO family photograph

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde criticised Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s Office for cropping Prime Minister Narendra Modi out of a photograph from the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit, saying Pakistan should not attempt to “play such games” with India.“What Pakistan has done is extremely unfortunate. Pakistan has always attempted such things. However, I would say that while they may have removed Modi Ji’s photograph, if Modi Ji wants, he can remove Pakistan from the world picture,” Shinde said on Tuesday.His remarks came after Sharif’s office shared an edited version of the SCO family photograph that placed the Pakistani prime minister at the centre while cropping out several leaders. The original photograph, taken before a session of the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek, showed the heads of member states standing together.“During Operation Sindoor, terrorists in Pahalgam committed a grave crime against our people and our sisters by wiping away their sindoor. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, our armed forces completely destroyed terrorist bases in Pakistan. They also destroyed 11 airbase camps and brought Pakistan to its knees,” he said.“The entire country is proud of the Indian armed forces and Prime Minister Modi’s leadership. Therefore, Pakistan should never attempt to play such games with our country,” Shinde added.He also said that editing Modi out of the photograph would not affect his standing in India or internationally.“I would also say that such an act of removing a photograph cannot erase Prime Minister Modi from the hearts of 140 crore Indians. In fact, Prime Minister Modi remains one of the most popular leaders in the world...”The 26th SCO summit, which marked the organisation’s 25th anniversary, focused on regional cooperation as well as security, economic and geopolitical challenges. The summit was held in the expanded “SCO Plus” format, bringing together leaders from member, partner and observer countries.Addressing the summit, PM Modi called for a united fight against terrorism and said there could be no “double standards” on the issue. He called for the dismantling of the “entire ecosystem of terrorism”, including its financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe havens.
Article Summary: Eknath Shinde criticised Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s Office for cropping Prime Minister Narendra Modi out of a photograph from the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. His remarks came after Sharif’s office shared an edited version of the SCO family photograph that placed the Pakistani prime minister at the centre while cropping out several leaders.

Article Title: 'They are from his film fan base': Congress MLA brushes aside TVK’s 'Vijay for PM' pitch

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert on Wednesday dismissed ally TVK’s projection of its leader, C Joseph Vijay, as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, saying TVK leaders were making the claim as “fans” of the chief minister, a reference to Vijay’s past as an actor.“They are TVK MLAs, they are all still in the fan basis. They have come from a fan--film industries as a fan basis. Definitely, they will be saying that,” Cuthbert told reporters in Chennai.She added that, politically, the leaders had taken a “stern decision” that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi would be the candidate for the prime minister’s post in 2029.Cuthbert’s remarks come amid growing differences over the political positioning of the two parties, with TVK leaders repeatedly projecting Vijay as a possible national leader.TVK leader and Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna had earlier asserted that the country’s top constitutional office should be held by a leader from Tamil Nadu.Responding to the remarks by TVK leaders, Congress leader and state Tourism Minister S Rajesh Kumar warned that the two Congress ministers in the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government would resign if the Vijay-led party did not accept Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate.The Congress ended its long-standing alliance with the DMK following the Tamil Nadu assembly elections in April and extended support to TVK, which emerged as the single-largest party but fell short of the majority mark. The Congress backed TVK along with the VCK, IUML, CPI and CPI(M), with the stated condition that “communal forces” be kept out of the government.Vijay launched TVK in February 2024, becoming the latest Tamil film star to enter state politics.The Congress last led a government at the Centre from 2004 to 2014.

Article Title: Northeast faces new vector threat as diseases spread to new areas: Health panel
Article Text:
Sikkim recorded the highest incidence among Northeast states, with 374 dengue cases in 2024. Using the state’s revised population estimate, the dengue incidence was 57.9 per lakh.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Climate change, deforestation, unplanned urbanisation and poor drainage are creating conditions for mosquitoes and other disease-carrying vectors to spread into new areas of the Northeast, a parliamentary health panel has warned, calling for targeted, technology-driven surveillance and prevention strategies.The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare, in its report on vector-borne diseases in North-East India, said the region's difficult terrain, changing rainfall and temperature patterns, rapid urbanisation and gaps in healthcare access were contributing to the persistence and geographical expansion of these diseases.The numbers show a sharp rise in dengue in the region. Reported cases increased from 142 in 2014 to 19,761 in 2023, before falling to 7,186 in 2024. The report records 1,524 cases in 2025 through August, making it a partial-year figure and therefore not directly comparable with full-year totals.Chikungunya cases in the region increased from 3,493 in 2023 to 3,991 in 2024, an increase of about 14.3%.The panel said dengue and chikungunya are increasingly urban concerns, driven by urbanisation, water-storage practices, poor waste management, climate change and population movement.Sikkim recorded the highest incidence among Northeast states, with 374 dengue cases in 2024. Using the state’s revised population estimate, the dengue incidence was 57.9 per lakh. Sikkim also reported 1,863 chikungunya cases, with an incidence of 291.2 per lakh in 2024.Malaria, however, presents a more mixed picture. Across India, the number of high-burden districts with an Annual Parasite Index above one fell from 155 in 2015 to 37 in 2024. In the Northeast, 16 districts in Arunachal Pradesh and six in Nagaland have reported zero indigenous malaria cases for the past three years.Japanese encephalitis remains another concern, particularly in Assam and other northeastern states. The report records 885 JE cases in the Northeast in 2024, compared with 709 in 2023. Nationally, the JE fatality rate fell substantially, from 17.6% in 2014 to 7.1% in 2024.The panel recommended real-time surveillance through a dedicated Northeast vector-borne disease portal and AI-based early-warning systems to predict hotspots, along with mobile health units, pre-monsoon camps, rapid-response teams, stronger labs and dedicated NESIDS funding for high-risk areas. It also called for disease-specific treatment protocols for severe dengue and other complications, a Regional Entomology Training Hub, and greater use of climate modelling and digital reporting. The panel flagged a data gap too: vector-borne disease data are not separately collected for tribal, rural and urban populations, and recommended doing so for more targeted interventions.
Article Summary: Climate change, deforestation, unplanned urbanisation and poor drainage are creating conditions for mosquitoes and other disease-carrying vectors to spread into new areas of the Northeast. The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare said the region's difficult terrain, changing rainfall and temperature patterns were contributing to the persistence and geographical expansion of these diseases.

Article Title: Ram temple cash theft: Journalist accuses cops of digital tracking
Article Text:
Abhishek Upadhyay on Tuesday sought Supreme Court's intervention

Abhishek Upadhyay, the journalist who reported embezzlement of donations at Ayodhya's Ram temple, on Tuesday sought Supreme Court's intervention saying that Ghaziabad police have, in connection with a case of road rage against him, sought his digital footprints from social media platform X since June 1, which could jeopardise identities of sources who tipped him about the donation scam.His counsel Anoop P Awasthi told a bench led by CJI Surya Kant that Ghaziabad police's request to X HQ in California for the alleged road rage case of Aug 18 would result in gross violation of his right to privacy, adding that such data in the hands of police would reveal the identities of the sources who informed him about temple theft.The FIR concerns an alleged incident of Aug 18, yet the investigating agency seeks the petitioner's IP and account-related information from June 1, well before the alleged incident. No nexus between such sweeping historical digital information and the investigation of the alleged incident has been disclosed in the impugned notice," Upadhyay said in his application.The bench said it had on Aug 25 protected the journalist from coercive action by police in the road rage case and that his fresh application would be listed for hearing in due course.
Article Summary: Abhishek Upadhyay reported embezzlement of donations at Ayodhya's Ram temple. Ghaziabad police have, in connection with a case of road rage against him, sought his digital footprints from social media platform X since June 1.

Article Title: Safai Karmachari Andolan counters govt reply in Parliament, claims manual scavenging still exists in atleast 46 districts
Article Text:
Muzaffar Ahmed Sheikh (35) from Ganderbal district in Jammu & Kashmir.

Mussi Devi (71) from Sitapur district in Uttar Pradesh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Challenging the Centre’s claim made in Parliament in the monsoon session that a survey conducted in all districts of the country during the year 2024-25 found no person engaged as a manual scavenger, Safai Karmachari Andolan (SKA) on Tuesday brought together women from Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and youth from Jammu & Kashmir claiming to be engaged in manual cleaning of human excreta in insanitary latrines to highlight that the illegal practice still persists in atleast 46 districts of these four states.National Convenor and co-founder of SKA, Bezwada Wilson said that they have evidence by way of photographs showing women lifting waste from dry latrines in these districts. “We will be writing to the ministry of social justice and empowerment to seek a fresh survey citing this evidence and demand action to stop the illegal practice in these districts within 60 days,” Wilson said.He, however, made it clear that if the ministry fails to act over the next two months, SKA teams will carry out a survey and put together a report by early next year. “We will highlight the findings across states and share them with Parliamentarians and the Judiciary to seek enforcement,” Wilson said.Former Supreme Court Judges Justice Madan Lokur and Justice Sudhandhu Dhulia and former Patna High Court Judge Justice Anjana Prakash expressed solidarity with the women and men who came forward to share heartwrenching experiences of a life marked by exploitation and untouchability despite the law in place wherein manual scavenging is illegal and dry latrines are banned.At the meeting held at Press Club of India as SKA announced the launch of a year long campaign ‘INDIA @ 80’ to free the country from manual scavenging, the former judges announced full support. Elaborating on the struggle by those involved in manual scavenging to break free, Justice Lokur expressed concern over the practice persisting despite the protection guaranteed by the Constitution of India against untouchability which is abolished and forbidden.He also dwelled on the long and continuing struggle for justice by those affected and how they have repeatedly ended up approaching the judiciary that has resulted in various directions from the Supreme Court from time to time. Justice Lokur highlighted that what is most worrying is the denial by authorities that the problem exists and the approach towards addressing the issue shows that ending the problem of manual scavenging is not a priority of the govt.He asserted that the govt must give priority to remove dry latrines wherever they remain. This he said should be a key focus area under the Swachh Bharat Mission.Justice Dhulia expressed shock that manual scavenging and dry latrines still exist in more than 40 districts and said that everyone must feel shame that such a practice continues to exist in our society.Justice Anjana Prakash too expressed concern over the lack of required efforts to end manual scavenging.As the workers shared their lived experiences as manual scavengers, one heard 71 - year - old Mussi Devi from Sitapur district in UP tell how her entire life has passed cleaning dry latrines and even now she is called by families in her area to manually clean-up and dispose of the waste. “When are we going to get freedom from this untouchability?,” asked Mussi Devi and others in her position. Ageing and frail, Devi is also the caregiver for her husband who is paralysed.35 - year - old Muzzafar Ahmed Sheikh from Jammu and Kashmir shared that he is the third generation in his family engaged in manual scavenging in dry latrines. He shared that his community is subjected to untouchability and even their houses are located in a separate cluster. He hails from Wussan village of Ganderbal. A father of a six - year - old, he says, “I want to break free from this identity of being a manual scavenger and I don’t want my son to grow up to do this ever. ”Bezwada Wilson summed up the sentiment of all those seeking justice. “I started the fight when I was 16 and now I am 60. Many things have changed but manual scavenging in dry latrines still remains. We have to end this menace without fail,” he asserted.It is pertinent to point that in the monsoon session of Parliament that concluded in August, in response to a written question in Lok Sabha by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, the minister of state for social justice and empowerment Ramdas Athawale said that as per the "Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (MS Act, 2013)", a fresh survey has been conducted in all districts of the country during the year 2024-25 in which no manual scavenger has been found. “All the districts of the country have completed the survey and declared themselves as manual scavengers' free,” he said.However, he also added that 58,098 Manual Scavengers (MS) have been identified during two earlier surveys conducted in 2013 and 2018.Clearly differentiating "manual scavenging" and "hazardous cleaning", the minister shared while the later pertains to manual cleaning of a sewer or septic tank, without the employer providing protective gear, cleaning devices and safety precautions, a manual scavenger is defined as someone employed for manually cleaning, carrying, disposing of human excreta in an insanitary latrine.
Article Summary: Safai Karmachari Andolan (SKA) brought together women from Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Jammu & Kashmir claiming to be engaged in manual cleaning of human excreta in insanitary latrines. The illegal practice still persists in atleast 46 districts of these four states. SKA announced the launch of a year long campaign ‘INDIA @ 80’ to free the country from manual scavenging.

Article Title: Bus gang-rape case: At minor’s UP village, locked house, silence and a family fleeing intrusion

AGRA: Fearing intrusion and social stigma, parents of the 17-year-old survivor in the Noida-Delhi bus gang-rape case have locked their house and left their UP village.A villager, who knows the family, toldon Tuesday: “After media persons began visiting our remote village in Mainpuri district seeking details about that horrific incident, they couldn’t take it anymore.” He added: “There’s no one in that house now, the dwelling has fallen silent. ”Another neighbour added: “No one here knew what had happened to the girl. When media persons came here on Monday and told us that she had been raped, everyone was shocked.” He appealed to journalists to avoid repeatedly visiting the place, citing concerns over the survivor’s future and privacy.“Please don’t come again and again to shoot videos or take pictures. She will have to get married in future. By revealing the village and asking people about her, the media has made the matter known here and also the neighbouring areas,” he added.The girl was allegedly sexually assaulted on a moving bus by the vehicle’s driver and conductor on Aug 4. The bus had travelled almost 50 km from Greater Noida to Old Delhi’s Kashmere Gate without being detected. The alleged sexual assault took place while she was travelling from Greater Noida towards Sector 63, police said.After violating her, the bus driver and conductor allegedly dumped her at Ring Road in the Kashmere Gate police station area. The accused duo were later identified as Kuldeep, 39 (bus driver); and Sandeep , 26 (conductor).The area’s SHO told: “The family is safe and have gone to their relatives.”Local MLA, who visited the village on Monday, said, “People in the village came to know about it probably yesterday. When I went there, I found her house locked. Her father’s phone was switched off. I made considerable efforts to speak with the family, but I have been unable to do so thus far.”The MLA added: “I demand the strictest possible punishment for the two accused.” Meanwhile, president of UP State Women Commission, Babita Chauhan, has written to police commissioner of Gautam Budh Nagar for “tough action”.

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Bombay high court orders CBI probe into Sushant Singh Rajput’s ex-manager’s death
Article Text:
The HC said a senior officer of the CBI to conduct the probe.

Also Read |

Also Read |





MUMBAI: Bombay high court on Wednesday pronounced its judgment in the Disha Salian case and directed registration of a first information report (FIR) for her June 8, 2020 death at a suburban Malad building in Mumbai.The Bombay HC appointed a senior officer of the CBI to conduct the probe. The HC also directed not to name anyone as accused in the FIR.“No one shall be treated as an accused unless and until there is suitable material against them, the HC directed.Salian, 28, was a celebrity manager and worked with the late film actor Sushant Singh who died just days later that month on June 14, aged 34 in his Bandra house.On Friday Justices SV Kotwal and RR Bhonsale had reserved for orders her father Satish Salian’s petition to probe her death as a murder arguing through his counsel Nilesh Ojha that “suspicious circumstances’ surrounded it.He had sought investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and said the HC did not lack powers to direct registration of an FIR and probe to ensure complete justice for her family.On Wednesday the HC said : The officer is attached to CBI senior officer in this case and register the FIR, no one be detained unless there's a reasonable suspicion raised, BNSS and Summary report be filed if nothing is found.”At a three day hearing the bench repeatedly questioned the State on why it was still conducting an inquiry under section 174 of the erstwhile criminal procedure code (CrPC)—a provision which it said had limited applicability. The purpose of section 174/175 is limited to ascertaining ‘cause of death’ , as the first line of probe on registration of an Accidental Death Report (ADR).The inquiry that was closed within three months was reopened in 2023 following social media claims, prompting the HC to question the validity of such an extended inquiry.The State represented by chief public prosecutor Shishir Hirey maintained her death was by suicide, following an alleged fall from allegedly the 12th floor of the residential building.Salian’s petition claimed former chief minister Uddhav Thackeray’s son Aditya Thackeray to be an alleged suspect. Salian’s counsel Ojha citing documents, alleged discrepancies and suspicious circumstances to seek a thorough probe as he argued a cognizable offence as claimed by her father, ought to be registered as an FIR as mandated by law.The HC on being shown documents including the Panchanama, photographs of the body, other details from the inquiry so far and raised questions on various aspects it said were “suspicious’’ including whether injuries were consistent with a fall from such height and details regarding clothes.Hirey argued that the injuries included a skull fracture consistent with such fall. Hirey also sought to justify the ADR level inquiry and submitted witness statements and forensics which he said ruled out foul play or any alleged sexual assault on her.The HC clarified that it was not drawing conclusions at this stage but questioned the what had State done for so long jn the last five years, when the prosecution sought dismissal of the father’s plea saying it was belatedly filed .Senior counsel Sudeep Pasbola appearing for Thackeray who had intervened in the matter said the State’s line of probe was not barred by law but also cannot extend indefinitely. Pasbola said Salian has an alternate remedy in law to first go to Magistrate with a private complaint if no FIR is registered and could not directly come to the HC. Pasbola also argued that allegations agaisnt Thackeray were “motivated’’ untenable and stem from a “political rivalry’’.The HC said it was concerned not with any political overtones but only with sanctity of law to provide the family a closure. Ojha argued since the plea was for CBI probe the HC had to be approached as a magistrate lacks the power to direct such probe.Four-and-a half years after it began probing the death of actor Sushant Singh Rajput, last March, the CBI was reported to have closed the case and given a clean chit to actor Rhea Chakraborty, bringing curtains on the case that had gripped the country in 2020.Last year Satish Salian also alleged his daughter was sexually assaulted and murdered and had approached HC seeking the CBI probe into her death as he also alleged both deaths are interconnected and part of a larger conspiracy.
Article Summary: The Bombay HC appointed a senior officer of the CBI to conduct the probe. The HC also directed not to name anyone as accused in the FIR. Justices SV Kotwal and RR Bhonsale had reserved for orders her father Satish Salian’s petition to probe her death as a murder.

Article Title: Times Square stabbing: Bank of America VP Erin Piacenti among victims
Article Text:
NYPD commissioner Jessica Tisch said the attack appeared to be random and unprovoked. Police said officers arriving at the scene encountered Pamela Cisneros, 49, who was brandishing two large knives and advancing towards them

Who was Erin Piacenti?

How the incident unfolded

A 32-year-old vice-president at Bank of America was killed in a stabbing incident in New York’s Times Square. The attack, described by police as “random” and unprovoked, unfolded on Monday afternoon.The victim was identified as Erin Piacenti, who was walking home from work when she was attacked near West 42nd Street and Seventh Avenue. Piacenti had recently returned to work after becoming a mother and had shared a photo of herself with her newborn daughter and husband four days before the stabbing.A 68-year-old man was also stabbed in the attack and was in stable condition, according to police. The attacker, identified as 49-year-old Pamela Cisneros, was shot and killed by officers after she advanced towards them while carrying two large knives.Piacenti was a vice-president in Bank of America’s Business Selection and Conflicts unit and had joined the company around 18 months ago, according to an internal memo and her LinkedIn profile.Matthew Koder, Bank of America’s president of Global Corporate & Investment Banking, described Piacenti as a “cherished teammate and friend” in an internal memo.“Erin was a valued member of the Business Selection and Conflicts team, having joined the bank 18 months ago,” Koder wrote.“Her loss is being felt deeply by many.”Bank of America confirmed Piacenti’s death and expressed condolences to her family.“We are shocked and deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague. She was a valued teammate who will be greatly missed. Our hearts go out to her family and all of her loved ones,” the bank said in a statement.Piacenti had earned a law degree from Fordham Law School, graduating in 2021 alongside her husband, Frank, according to the school. Fordham Law said in a statement it was heartbroken by her death.Bank of America’s Manhattan office is located at One Bryant Park, just a few blocks from the site of the stabbing.NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said the attack appeared to be random and unprovoked. Police identified the attacker as Pamela Cisneros, 49, of Queens.According to Tisch, Cisneros pulled two knives from a shopping bag, stabbed the 68-year-old man and then attacked Piacenti. When officers arrived, they found Cisneros brandishing two large knives and advancing towards them.Officers used a stun gun and tried to persuade her to drop the weapons for several minutes, but she refused. Tisch said Cisneros told officers she “would rather kill” them. Two officers then shot her, and she was later pronounced dead.Tisch said Cisneros had a documented mental health history, with police encounters related to mental health in 2018 and 2019, but no arrest record in New York City.Cisneros’ brother, Patrick Peralta, told Gothamist that she had psychiatric problems for decades but was not aggressive. He said she had been taking medication and had been doing better in recent years, working on and off in a legal office.“We really don’t know how to express or how to explain why this happened," Peralta told Gothamist, expressing sympathy for Piacenti’s family and the injured man.Koder said Bank of America’s security teams were “fully engaged in supporting the police investigation here, and in addressing the ongoing safety and security of our offices and teammates”.
Article Summary: Erin Piacenti, 32, was walking home from work when she was attacked near West 42nd Street and Seventh Avenue. A 68-year-old man was also stabbed in the attack and was in stable condition, according to police. Police identified the attacker as Pamela Cisneros, 49, of Queens. She was shot and killed by officers after she advanced towards them while carrying two large knives.

Article Title: ‘Pre-event indications’: Did Nepal miss warning signs before deadly floods? What report says
Article Text:
A visual from the flash floods that has killed over 1,100

Also Read |

Warning signs before collapse?

Also Read |

Death toll rises to 1,127

Other reports also highlighted disaster possibility

The glacier collapse that triggered a devastating landslide and flash floods along the Nepal-China border, killing over 1,100 showed visible signs of instability days before the disaster, according to a new report by the HiRISK scientific consortium.Scientists said there were “pre-event indications”, including meltwater that had turned visibly brown and signs of a crack propagating into the surrounding bedrock slope.The findings have raised fresh questions over the lack of operational early warning systems for glacier-related hazards in the remote Himalayan region, with scientists saying more comprehensive systems downstream could have saved a “significant number of lives”.The HiRISK report, published last week, cited by CNN, examined the physical changes preceding the glacier collapse and the potential for early detection.“In hindsight, there were some pre-event indications,” the scientists said, pointing to visibly brown meltwater and a crack that was propagating into the surrounding bedrock slope days before the collapse.However, detecting such changes in a remote, high-altitude environment remains difficult.The report said early warning systems had recently been established in the region to monitor several glacial lakes in China, but no operational system was in place specifically for glacier-related hazards in the area where the collapse occurred.Once the collapse began, the speed of the initial landslide meant conventional warning systems would likely have provided too little time to evacuate a border checkpoint that was among the first areas hit.Further downstream, however, there may have been more time to respond.The scientists said comprehensive early warning systems capable of providing 10 minutes or more of advance notice could have saved a “significant number of lives”.The finding stressed the need for systems that can monitor not only glacial lakes but also unstable glaciers and surrounding mountain slopes, while ensuring warnings reach vulnerable communities downstream.As the cause and rescue ops continue, 1,127 people have died in the floods, according to Nepal Police. A total of 45 bodies have been recovered from Rasuwa, 155 from Nuwakot, 59 from Dhading, 348 from Chitwan, 66 from Gorkha, 38 from Tanahun, 217 from Nawalparasi East and 190 from Nawalparasi West.The death toll has risen to 1,127, with 45 bodies recovered in Rasuwa, 155 in Nuwakot, 59 in Dhading, 348 in Chitwan, 66 in Gorkha, 38 in Tanahun, 217 in Nawalparasi East and 190 in Nawalparasi West. Nine bodies have also been recovered in India. So far, only 95 of the total recovered bodies have been identified and handed over to their families.The disaster has also renewed calls for greater cooperation between Nepal and China in monitoring hazards across the Himalayas.Chinese and Nepali authorities had met as recently as May to discuss strengthening cooperation on monitoring natural hazards in the region, according to a government official who attended the meeting.Experts say better cross-border information sharing is particularly important because mountain hazards can rapidly affect communities and infrastructure on either side of the border.“There is almost no way that anyone could have detected this event prior – it happened in a blind spot … (making it) extremely difficult to detect,” Austin Lord, a senior fellow in the Energy, Water and Sustainability programme at the Stimson Center, wrote in a recent commentary.He also highlighted “how greater communication, information sharing, and collaborative analysis of transboundary risks between Nepal and China are sorely needed.”India also stepped up to assist Nepal’s rescue operations, deploying specialised Army teams to work alongside Nepali forces at the Chilime and Langtang tunnel sites. The teams have been navigating difficult terrain and unstable conditions as they search for missing people.Read more: India steps in with emergency helplines for stranded nationals The HiRISK report is separate from two major reports released by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) in March 2026.The ICIMOD reports examined longer-term changes across the Hindu Kush Himalaya and warned that accelerating glacier loss was increasing the risks of cryosphere-related hazards, including glacial lake outburst floods.They found that HKH glaciers lost around 12 per cent of their total area and 9 per cent of their estimated ice reserves between 1990 and 2020, while glacier ice loss had doubled after 2000.The reports also found that the region’s smallest glaciers were shrinking particularly rapidly, with three-fourths of HKH glaciers falling into the vulnerable category of less than 0.5 square kilometres.ICIMOD also highlighted major gaps in glacier monitoring. Its 2026 Glacier Outlook found that only seven of 38 monitored glaciers met the global benchmark monitoring standards set by the World Glacier Monitoring Service, while several major glacierised regions remained largely unmonitored.“This isn’t a distant problem; it’s a crisis unfolding in real-time, with new disasters every summer and monsoon,” ICIMOD Director General Pema Gyamtsho said.Thus, the ICIMOD reports provided a broad assessment of the region’s accelerating glacier loss and the risks it creates, while the new HiRISK report focuses specifically on the recent disaster, including the physical warning signs before the collapse and whether early warning systems could have reduced casualties.
Article Summary: Scientists say there were “pre-event indications’, including meltwater that had turned visibly brown and signs of a crack propagating into the surrounding bedrock slope. The findings have raised fresh questions over the lack of operational early warning systems for glacier-related hazards in the Himalayas.

Article Title: Started by a Muslim, a Kolkata Janmashtami turns ‘Hindu-only’
Article Text:

KOLKATA: One of Kolkata’s more prominent Janmashtami celebrations in Mominpore — where most of the organisers have been Muslims, making it an example of the city’s multi-cultural spirit — is set to turn into a Hindu-only affair this year.Rakesh Singh, who was BJP ’s (losing) candidate from the Port assembly constituency this year, toldon Tuesday that the celebrations will be organised by “only Hindus” this year as Janmashtami is “a Hindu festival”.Singh, who counted himself as a Congress functionary and used to control Alipore zoo’s labour union as part of the Indian National Trade Union Congress (a Congress affiliate), said he believes in Vishwa Hindu Parishad ’s ideology that “religion belongs to individuals and festivals also belong to those individuals” and was critical of former CM Mamata Banerjee’s oft-repeated statement that “religion belongs to individuals but festivals belong to everyone”.This Janmashtami event, held at the Bhukailash Road-Hussain Shah Road crossing in Kolkata Municipal Corporation’s Ward 79 — part of the Port assembly constituency and bordering CM Suvendu Adhikari’s and former CM Mamata Banerjee’s Bhowanipore constituency — enters its 58th year this time. Prominent patrons have included former city mayor Firhad Hakim and senior Trinamool functionaries Mohammed Alam and Serajul Karim.Singh’s “takeover” of the celebrations comes about a week after VHP addressed the city’s Durga Puja organisers on how to conduct Bengal’s biggest festival. Among the dos and don’ts listed were that there should be no distortion of deities’ images and pandals should be designed to maintain Hindu culture and heritage. VHP also asked puja organisers to strictly prohibit non-vegetarian food inside the core pandal area citing the need to maintain spiritual purity and cleanliness.Singh, who claimed to be both president and chairperson of the Janmashtami organising committee, said, “We cannot demean our traditional culture. People from other religions should definitely visit pandals but it is our duty to protect our religious activities. Janmashtami is a Hindu festival and it should be performed by Hindus only.”According to locals, the Janmashtami event, which is organised by Kidderpore Samaj Kalyan Samity, was initiated by a Muslim social worker, Md Kashim, about six decades ago but faded over the years till another group of Muslim youths revived it after Trinamool came to office in 2011.“Since 2011, we have been organising Janmashtami here. There were around 20 members in the organising committee, and half of them were Muslims. We used to celebrate the event together, distribute prasad and ensure all rituals were followed. But this year, all Muslim faces have been kept out of the committee,” said Md Alam, a Trinamool functionary and former office-bearer of the organising committee.On Monday,found a huge saffron-and-white pandal being erected at the venue. “Muslims used to control Janmashtami here till last year. But this year, it will be exclusively conducted and managed by Hindus. It’s like a cleansing activity,” said an organiser overseeing the pandal construction.
Article Summary: Rakesh Singh, who was BJP ’s (losing) candidate from the Port assembly constituency this year, toldon Tuesday that the celebrations will be organised by ‘only Hindus’ Singh said he believes in Vishwa Hindu Parishad’s ideology that ‘religion belongs to individuals and festivals also belong to those individuals’

Article Title: Meet Aditi Paudel, a 17-year-old high school student appointed as Japan's first literacy ambassador
Article Text: Born in Japan, and raised in Nepal during her early childhood, Aditi Paudel had always shown an affinity towards reading. Her earliest memory of reading is of her grandfather handing her a newspaper filled with intricate Devanagari script when she was still in preschool. But to the surprise of those around her, she was still able to make sense of the text. Over the years, she has only improved and the now 17-year-old high school senior in Tokyo was recently appointed as Japan's first literacy ambassador, as per a report by The Japan Times.The World Literacy Foundation, a global nonprofit headquartered in Australia is running a program where around 900 young people between the ages of 16 and 25 from 101 countries are participating. While the program has been running for 12 years, this is the first time an ambassador from Japan has been appointed, according to Andrew Kay, CEO and founder of the World Literacy Foundation.The aim of the program is to connect young people around the world and get them “involved and waving the flag for literacy in their community,” Kay said, noting that Paudel was singled out “for her leadership, passion for literacy, and commitment to empowering young people in Japan.”“Her curiosity about English shaped thoughtful advocacy, strengthening the program’s global voice and cultural reach,” he added.Paudel returned to Japan to enter the third grade and along with settling into a new life, she found herself having to learn Japanese once more, which meant turning to the books. Her love for reading came pretty early in her life, nurtured by her father who bought her plenty of books. She developed an early taste for fantasy, and recalled falling in love with Enid Blyton’s “The Wishing-Chair.”Reading Malala Yousafzai 's autobiography, 'I Am Malala', helped her develop significant interests in female empowerment, including ensuring that women across the world have access to education and literacy. Along with working with children with disabilities, she plans to work with the Shanti Volunteer Association to collect and donate books to Asian countries with lower rates of literacy, including Nepal.With enough experience developing her own reading skills, Paudel said that a common view of literacy is how well a person can read or write, but she sees it in broader terms. Essentially, it’s “something that helps you open doors for more opportunities,” she noted.Paudel has experienced the impact of her access to private education firsthand and how it has set her life on a different course. “My parents grew up in a completely opposite environment. They did not have a childhood like this,” she said. “Being literate is so important because even though you have the potential, you can never unlock it if you do not have literacy.”But even those with easy access to books are reading less than they once did. Around half of elementary, junior high and high school age children in Japan do not read books, according to a recent study by Benesse Educational Research & Development Institute and the University of Tokyo.Fewer young people are reading for pleasure and enjoyment, said Kay, and that could cause a significant regressive effect. “As far as embedding themselves in a novel or reading something that really takes a little bit more effort, that is becoming a rarer thing,” he said. Kay also cautions against the impact of artificial intelligence, noting that the latest tech tools provide quick answers, allowing people to skip the process of researching, reading and wrestling with theories and thoughts oneself.“It’s turning our clock back 150 years … where most people couldn’t read or would have limited ability to read,” he said of the absence of reading books as a mainstream pursuit. Those trends only add importance to initiatives like the World Literacy Foundation’s ambassador program.As a teenager, Paudel understands what it is like to grow up surrounded by distractions, with much of life centred around social media. “You will always be more inclined to go for your phone rather than a book,” she said. That is why she believes building a reading habit is important. Her advice is not to work through a list of classic books, but to find something that connects with you. Ideally, she said, reading should also help broaden your perspective.
Article Summary: Aditi Paudel, a 17-year-old high school senior in Tokyo, was recently appointed as Japan's first literacy ambassador. The World Literacy Foundation, a global nonprofit headquartered in Australia is running a program where around 900 young people between the ages of 16 and 25 from 101 countries are participating.

Article Title: Nepal floods bring 'unusual' fish to Bihar, govt warns people not to eat or sell them
Article Text:
A large unusual fish caught in the floodwaters of the Gandak basin being examined by locals at Valmikinagar in West Champaran

BETTIAH: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into the Gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from Nepal have prompted the Bihar govt to issue a safety advisory, asking residents of West Champaran and Gopalganj not to consume or trade in such fish until their identity and safety are confirmed.The fisheries division of the dairy, fisheries and animal resources department issued the caution on Tuesday after unusual fish were found in local water bodies and low-lying areas across the flood-hit Gandak basin.Floodwaters from Nepal have entered the Gandak system, inundating several areas of West Champaran and Gopalganj. The department said fish can be swept away from ponds, rivers and other water bodies during floods and carried over considerable distances. During this movement, they may come into contact with contaminated drains, dead animals and other pollutants, raising the risk of contamination by bacteria, viruses and fungi.“Do not consume any unidentified or unusual-looking fish. Until confirmation by the concerned department, an unfamiliar fish should not be considered fit for consumption,” the advisory said.Residents have also been asked not to buy or sell unfamiliar fish caught from floodwaters or assume an unusual-looking species is safe merely because it resembles a commonly eaten fish.Anyone developing vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dizziness or breathing difficulty after consuming such fish has been advised to seek immediate medical attention.Wildlife Trust of India director Sameer Kumar Sinha said most fish swept into the Gandak in Bihar following the Nepal floods are believed to be ‘Bagarius bagarius’, commonly known as the goonch catfish and locally called “Gochita”.He said the large freshwater catfish is found in fast-flowing rivers of India, Nepal and parts of Southeast Asia. The carnivorous species feeds on smaller fish, crabs and other aquatic organisms and often hides among rocks in deep stretches with strong currents.Sinha said local communities consume the fish, but it spoils quickly after death and may pose health risks if eaten after deterioration. He urged people to follow the Bihar govt advisory and exercise caution. The species is listed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as threatened.
Article Summary: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into Gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from Nepal have prompted Bihar govt to issue safety advisory. Residents of West Champaran and Gopalganj not to consume or trade in such fish until their identity and safety are confirmed.

Article Title: Pak takes SCO chair, PM Modi slams use of terror as strategic asset
Article Text:
Modi said countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy must be sent a strong message

Also Read:

Framing security as a non-negotiable prerequisite for regional progress, PM Narendra Modi delivered a thinly veiled warning to Pakistan over state-sponsored terrorism at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. With Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif in attendance, Modi said countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy, and provide shelter and support to terrorists, must be sent a strong message that terrorism can never be a strategic asset for anyone.The remarks are significant also because of the timing. Pakistan assumed rotating chairmanship of SCO from Kyrgyzstan on Tuesday and will host the heads-of-state summit next year, for which it will invite Modi, along with others.Modi made the remarks, in which he also warned against double standards on terrorism, while expanding on India's SCO vision - Security, Connectivity and Opportunity - that he articulated in Tianjin last year.With Chinese President Xi Jinping also present, PM reiterated India's position that all connectivity initiatives must respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states as this is also the "fundamental spirit" of SCO charter.Modi said that terrorism continued to pose a serious challenge to humanity and it's important to not remain confined to an action-reaction approach in the fight against the menace.“We must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorist financing, recruitment, radicalisation, and safe havens. We must speak with one voice and make it clear that there can be no place for double standards on this serious issue,” said PM, without naming Pakistan as SCO charter doesn’t allow members to raise bilateral differences.India and Pakistan together joined the China-dominated Eurasian grouping as full members in 2017. For India, the security-oriented SCO has served as a platform not just to assert its strategic autonomy but also flag regional risks from state-sponsored terrorism. Modi said that the bloc’s shared aspiration for a peaceful and secure Eurasia is also closely linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan and that India will continue to contribute to the development and provision of humanitarian assistance to people of the country.Modi addressed West Asia crisis, saying it was affecting energy security, maritime trade and supply chains around the world and recalling his message earlier that conflicts cannot be resolved on the battlefield. “Countries of Global South bear greatest brunt of such disruptions. Therefore, India has consistently called for all tensions and conflicts to be resolved not on battlefield, but through dialogue and diplomacy,” he added.While underlining the importance India attaches to SCO, Modi said that at a time when the world is passing through instability, the organisation must transform the shared geography into opportunities and bring about positive change in people’s lives. Describing SCO as a confluence of great civilisations, cultures, and ideas, he said that over next 25 years, people-to-people ties should remain at the heart of cooperation among the member states.“True measure of our success should be how many new opportunities our efforts create, how many new markets open up for entrepreneurs, how much farmers benefit from tech, and how much better the lives of our citizens become,” said the PM. According to an Indian readout of PM’s participation, Modi stated that strong and trusted connectivity initiatives were important for the group’s shared progress and prosperity.“Underlining that India supports connectivity efforts that link markets, enhance trade and open new opportunities for development, he reiterated such efforts should respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of nations,” said the readout.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi delivered a thinly veiled warning to Pakistan over state- sponsored terrorism at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. With Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif in attendance, Modi said countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy, and provide shelter and support to terrorists, must be sent a strong message.

Article Title: Barefoot mom in sari runs 3km to win Rs 5k for kids' education
Article Text:
Ramabai ran 3km with the indomitable spirit of a mother competing for a cash prize

PUNE: Ramabai Ranvir had no idea what running a race meant. All she had heard was there was Rs 3,000 to be won if she finished first.So, the 47-year-old widow hopped onto the pickup with a group of police aspirants from the Beed academy where she worked, hoping to compete in what would be the first race of her life. It didn't bother her that she hadn't trained for the rigours of a long-distance run. It hardly mattered that she was the lone runner without shoes.In her sari, barefoot after her slippers gave up midway through the run, Ramabai ran 3km with the indomitable spirit of a mother competing for a cash prize that would ease her struggle to pay for her daughters' education."I ran like my life depended on it. I didn't know how much time I needed to cover the distance. I only sto-pped once I was past the finish line," she told TOI. "I am so happy they gave me Rs 5,000 instead of Rs 3,000. I bought notebooks and pens for my daughter Pooja. The remaining money is for Arti."Ramabai works in the kitchen at Dnyandeep Acad-emy, making over 200 chapatis a day for a monthly salary of Rs 9,000.The native of Potra, Hingoli, took the job to fund the education of her two daughters after her husband died in 2012.On Aug 28, her younger daughter Arti (20), a BSc computer science student who lives alone in Nanded, called asking for money for food and rent. Ramabai, who didn't have any cash to spare, had a sleepless night.At dawn, she heard the academy's trainers rounding up aspirants for a running competition nearby. She instantly decided to join in."There is no pain worse than that of not being able to take care of your children. The moment I came to know of the race, winning was the only thing on my mind."Datta Darade, who heads the academy, said Ramabai's determination moved him. The academy had enrolled her elder daughter Pooja (22) free of cost and given her employment and a room to stay in. "I was taking my students to the marathon. When Ramabai said she wanted to come along, I asked her, 'What will you do there?' She said, 'I will run.' I couldn't believe it when she won in the above-30 category."Pooja finished second in the 18-30 age group and won Rs 2,000. Arti said she was dumbstruck when her sister called to say their mother had won."Our mother studied till Class 7 and has worked all her life, not taking breaks even when she was unwell. She didn't hesitate to send me to Nanded for my studies. I am not surprised she decided to win a race for her family," she said.
Article Summary: Ramabai Ranvir ran 3km with the indomitable spirit of a mother competing for a cash prize. The 47-year-old widow works in the kitchen at Dnyandeep Acad-emy, making over 200 chapatis a day for a monthly salary of Rs 9,000.

Article Title: PM Modi repeats call to 'shun unnecessary gold buys, foreign weddings & holidays'
Article Text:
PM Modi on Tuesday lauded Indian economy's resilience during a period of global crises

NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the better-than-expected GDP growth, PM Modi on Tuesday lauded Indian economy's resilience during a period of global crises. He again pushed for swadeshi goods and urged citizens to shun overseas weddings, foreign vacations and avoid unnecessary gold purchases at a time when imports remain elevated due to high commodity prices in the wake of the West Asia conflict.His appeal against buying gold also puts to rest speculation around import duties being reviewed by govt. In fact, Centre and RBI are keeping a close watch on shipments. Since Jan, both quantity of gold and value of imports have increased. Since Modi's first appeal in May, however, there has been a drop in quantity of imports but the value of imports is rising due to higher prices, albeit at a slower pace. At $3.5 a kg, the unit value of gold was 94% higher in June, but prices have moderated to $2.8 a kg, which was 47% more than a year ago.Since Modi’s first appeal in May, gold import quantity has dropped, but import value is rising due to higher prices, albeit slower. Prices moderated to $2.8 a kg, 47% more than a year ago.While gold remains an investment option for households, higher prices have deterred consumers from buying large quantities, with recycling of old jewellery also rising, industry executives said.Modi also mounted a withering attack on LoP Rahul Gandhi for spreading pessimism about growth, dismissing his criticism as “jhooth ki goonj”.This was Modi’s second reaction to the growth rate within 24 hours. His message mixed praise for people’s hard work with disdain for critics like Rahul and reiterated his call to citizens to avoid non-essential gold purchases and foreign trips.“We have to maintain this pace and keep growing and, for this, aatmanirbhar Bharat is essential,” he said in a selfie-video posted on Instagram.GDP grew at 7.8% in the April-June quarter, bringing relief to the NDA govt, which has been buffeted by the opposition parties, especially Congress under Rahul, over alleged misgovernance. Modi said, “There are people within India who are mired in despair, ‘jhooth ki goonj’, and are busy spreading pessimism everywhere.”Emphasising India’s feat, Modi said it came amid global conflicts and crises, causing supply-chain disruption. Since Covid in 2020, stability has remained elusive for the world but India is progressing at a fast pace, he added.Opposition has a right to criticise govt but especially Congress shouldn’t insult people by being incorrigible naysayers and call India a dead economy when data speaks otherwise, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said.BJP played up Rahul’s dismissive comments about the economy to contrast them with India’s growth. Besides his dead economy jibe, Rahul claimed a crisis unseen in people’s lifetime would hit the economy. An economic tsunami was coming, he had said. Modi said his govt’s policy is right and intentions clear, calling upon people to work hard. India’s collective strength will take it to new heights. By emphasising swadeshi and self-reliance, people will bequeath a developed India to the young generation.At a press conference, BJP’s Ravi Shankar Prakash demanded Rahul apologise. As leader of opposition, Rahul’s comments carry weight, he said. The world has begun taking them lightly as he makes misleading remarks, while Pakistan plays them up.

He again pushed for swadeshi goods and urged citizens to shun overseas weddings, foreign vacations and avoid unnecessary gold purchases. His appeal against buying gold also puts to rest speculation around import duties being reviewed by govt. Since Jan, both quantity of gold and value of imports have increased.

Article Title: Translating the Reliance ethos into a blueprint for nation-building
Article Text:
Translating familial empathy into enterprise resilience

Democratising technology for a billion aspirations

Reclaiming soft power and passing the baton

There is a prevailing wisdom in global business schools that suggests the larger an enterprise grows, the colder it must become. Scale, the theory goes, demands a clinical detachment. Yet, in the heart of India's corporate landscape, a remarkably different experiment has been playing out for decades. Here, the traditional Indian family ethos has not been discarded as an archaic social structure but rather leveraged as a sophisticated business strategy.The recently released Reliance documentary, 'Parvah Hai Toh Parivar Hai', pulls back the curtain on this machinery. It offers a case study of what happens when the ethics of a household extend to a conglomerate employing hundreds of thousands, and ultimately to a nation of 1.4 billion people.Stripping away the complex financial jargon often associated with India's largest enterprise, the film reveals a foundational philosophy rooted in care, trust, and self-reliance. It asks a compelling question: can familial empathy actually drive a nation's socio-economic trajectory?At the corporate level, this paternalistic model is far more than a warm metaphor. It operates as a highly effective structural framework. The fundamental premise that care defines a family dictates how the company handles its human capital. During moments of intense crisis, such as health emergencies or natural disasters, this responsibility translates into the swift mobilisation of healthcare, isolation facilities, and emergency resources.This culture of protective support builds a rare institutional resilience, fostering a fiercely loyal ecosystem. Recalling the early days of setting up Jio Studios, an executive describes the deep personal involvement of the leadership. "I remember Mukesh Bhai and Manoj Bhai laying out their vision for the media business," she notes. "I remember thinking, do I have to pay to work here because this kind of mentorship is something that money cannot buy. "When creative and professional ventures face unexpected headwinds, this cushion of corporate confidence remains largely intact. Actor Ranveer Singh, reflecting on his collaborations with the conglomerate, highlighted this unusual patience. "I was given all the love, all the support and all the encouragement even at a time when my movies were not doing well," he shares in the film. "Career ups and downs. But to have received that kind of support meant a lot to me. It's nothing short of a blessing, an honour and a privilege to be associated with the Ambani family."However, the true test of any family-led business model lies in its ability to step outside its own perimeter and serve the wider community. For Reliance, modern nation building has meant translating massive corporate capacity into accessible public utility. Having already rewired India's digital landscape by making high-speed data universal through Jio, the enterprise is now looking towards the next frontier.The leadership frequently questions how their scale affects the masses. According to the documentary, the next step involves using new age technologies to bridge socio-economic gaps. "How does it affect the 1.4 billion people of India as we democratise information," the film asks, noting that generative artificial intelligence is "now democratising intelligence amongst 1.4 billion people."The ambition is to create tools that serve every stratum of society. The narrative paints a stark rural reality, envisioning a person in Bhagalpur "able to really use an AI tutor to teach himself or a farmer who is able to really understand what his food productivity would be." As the leadership points out, with this knowledge, "he is able to think more, he is able to do more, he is able to earn more and that is I think the ultimate goal for us. "Recognising that there are many Indias cutting across different income classes, the company is pivoting toward voice-first interfaces designed for the country's vast linguistic diversity. The documentary rightly points out that "Indians actually converse with technology by voice first rather than text." It is framed as a massive opportunity "which truly only an Indian company can solve." This ethos of mass accessibility comes directly from the top. As Mukesh Ambani directed his team regarding their massive streaming footprint: "The business is always important but I want consumers to experience our innovation."Beyond digital infrastructure, nation building requires fierce cultural stewardship. This household-led framework views corporate success as a catalyst for preserving national identity. Noting that foreign companies have historically dominated the sector, the documentary asserts, "There was no reason why an Indian company should not be leading the charts on media."Through Jio Studios, the mandate is bold: "What we want to do is claim back the narrative of India, especially young India." By backing massive commercial cinema alongside globally recognised projects, the conglomerate is actively shaping India's cultural footprint. Furthermore, spaces like the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre serve a dual purpose. "The vision of Mrs. Ambani and the vision of our centre is bringing the best of the world to India and the best of India to the world," the film notes.As the company approaches its 50th year, it stands at a critical juncture. Mukesh Ambani frames this generational shift not as a standard corporate handover, but as a continuation of core values. "Akash, Isha and Anant are only representatives of the young leaders," he explains. "And they will take our values. They will build an India of our dreams."At its heart, the enterprise remains anchored by its dining table roots. "To me, family is everything. I feel privileged that four generations of our family live together," shares Nita Ambani. This restless drive is perhaps best captured by 88-year-old V. Balasubramanian, who has spent 62 years at Reliance. He shares, "When I go away from this world, Dhirubhai is waiting there. We will start another Reliance Industries there and start working there and building up another empire. "Ultimately, the Reliance narrative suggests that India's economic rise is deeply intertwined with business models that align commercial scale with societal care. By treating a nation as an extended family, the company offers a compelling, distinctly Indian blueprint for modern nation building.
Article Summary: Reliance documentary, 'Parvah Hai Toh Parivar Hai', pulls back the curtain on this machinery. It offers a case study of what happens when the ethics of a household extend to a conglomerate employing hundreds of thousands, and ultimately to a nation of 1.4 billion people.

Article Title: Srinagar ghost mall turns into Rs 422cr jewel in auction
Article Text:
Srinagar’s stalled commercial complex fetched an eye-popping Rs 421.75 crore (Representative image)

SRINAGAR: For years, grass and weeds had more business at Sangarmaal City Centre than shoppers did. Then came the bidders. A 45-kanal (5.625 acre) parcel around Srinagar’s stalled commercial complex fetched an eye-popping Rs 421.75 crore after an overnight auction far exceeded what govt had pegged.Bidding opened at 11am on Aug 25 for land in front of and behind Sangarmaal, just behind Kashmir Golf Course and opposite Polo View, a pedestrian-only high-street market lined with cafes and boutique stores. One end of the property touches Chunt Khul, a stream running through Srinagar. Dal Lake is about 1km away. Lal Chowk is within easy reach.That mix of location, scale and commercial potential made this largely underused land a prized piece of real estate.By 1.48am on Aug 26, Sangarmaal became one of J&K’s hottest pieces of public real estate, with officials watching the price race far beyond their Rs 200-crore expectations. The highest bid touched Rs 421.75 crore on a full-lease basis.“My heart was racing as the bid was going up and up. It is an important project for J&K and this bid will open investment in the Union Territory after a long time,” an official said Tuesday.Parmesh Construction Company Ltd, a consortium of Pahalgam Green Hotels, a J&K firm and Bhutani Infra Ltd, emerged as the successful bidder.Sangarmaal City Centre traces its roots to 2015, when then CM Mufti Mohammad Sayeed announced it as a new commercial venture meant to give Srinagar a modern skyline.What emerged was an ambitious complex with landscaped areas, fountains, basement and surface parking, lifts and escalators. Its commercial inventory included 62 shops in the main commercial module, 38 spaces in Craft Bazaar, 11 kiosks, two food courts, a restaurant and 11 office spaces.But the dream never got off the ground. Most shops stayed shut. Buyers who acquired units did not open them. Weeds overran the premises, turning what was meant to be a bustling commercial hub into a near-deserted property.Now, a fresh lease could mean a fresh start. The front and rear portions have been offered for development on a full-lease basis, with a multiplex and other commercial facilities proposed.The Sangarmaal auction also set the stage for another high-stakes property bid. At Batamaloo, about 6km away, roughly 70 kanals (8.75 acre) of bus-stand land has remained largely underused and vulnerable to encroachment. Srinagar Development Authority (SDA) is seeking to redevelop it for better use.Bidding opened at Rs 95 crore on Aug 27 and climbed to Rs 305 crore by evening, with Construction Engineers, another J&K consortium, emerging as highest bidder. Batamaloo is also being offered on a full-lease basis, with plans for shopping, office spaces and housing.
Article Summary: A 45-kanal (5.625 acre) parcel around Srinagar’s stalled commercial complex fetched an eye-popping Rs 421.75 crore after an overnight auction. Sangarmaal City Centre traces its roots to 2015, when then CM Mufti Mohammad Sayeed announced it as a new commercial venture.

Article Title: Tribunal alters gay ex-IAF man 'dismissal' to 'routine discharge'
Article Text:
Instead of granting the discharge, IAF initiated a court of inquiry

NEW DELHI: The principal bench of Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) has converted the order of dismissal of a non-commissioned IAF officer, who confessed to being gay, into a routine discharge.The bench, headed by Justice Rajendra Menon and Justice Rasika Chaube, ruled that substituting dismissal with routine discharge prevents lasting career stigma for the ex-officer seeking employment outside the armed forces.The non-commissioned IAF officer, who had served about 10 and a half years, had applied for a compassionate premature discharge in 2024 to settle down with his partner, disclosing his relationship in an application.Instead of granting the discharge, IAF initiated a court of inquiry. The inquiry concluded he had breached discipline and risked national security by entering into a relationship with a foreigner. The court of inquiry also found him guilty of travelling abroad (Thailand and Sri Lanka) without permission. He was subsequently dismissed from service earlier this year.He then approached AFT principal bench not to challenge IAF's disciplinary right, but to request "dismissal" be changed to a "discharge" so he could seek future civilian employment.The bench held that while dismissal is warranted when rules are breached, exceptions must be considered in this case. "The respondents could have granted discharge to the applicant, but in the garb of maintaining discipline they dismissed him. The effect of both is identical inasmuch as the respondents do not want the service of the applicant."
Article Summary: The bench, headed by Justice Rajendra Menon and Justice Rasika Chaube, ruled that substituting dismissal with routine discharge prevents lasting career stigma. The non-commissioned IAF officer had served about 10 and a half years. He had applied for a compassionate premature discharge in 2024 to settle down with his partner, disclosing his relationship in an application.

Article Title: India on board, SCO reiterates condemnation of Iran attacks
Article Text:
SCO member-states, including India, reiterated the bloc's condemnation of military strikes on Iranian territory

India also joined other member-states in expressing condolences over the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Expressing deep concern over developments in "the Middle East and around Iran", the SCO member-states including India reiterated the bloc's condemnation of military strikes on Iranian territory that resulted in numerous civilian casualties and significant damage to Iran's economy, said the Bishkek Declaration.India also joined other member-states in expressing condolences over the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei.This was the second time that the SCO denounced the strikes on Iran after the West Asia war started on February 28, the first in an early March standalone statement that called the attacks unacceptable. India had endorsed that statement too, even though bilaterally it has not explicitly condemned the attacks on Iran the way it has missile and drone strikes on the GCC countries.However, unlike the Tianjin Declaration last year that too condemned the June 2025 US and Israeli strikes on Iran, the Bishkek Declaration did not name the US and Israel."Such actions violate the principles and norms of international law and the UN Charter and create serious risks to international peace, security and stability," said SCO's Bishkek Declaration.India and others backed Iran's sovereignty and territorial integrity, advocating a resolution to the conflict solely through political and diplomatic means.In this regard, they welcome all efforts aimed at de-escalating the situation in the region and, as the declaration said, noted that the only possible way to ensure peace and stability in the Middle East is a comprehensive and just settlement of the Palestinian question.PM Narendra Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the margins of the SCO summit in Bishkek on Monday and backed expansion of bilateral economic ties with Tehran, while the Iranian president sought India's help to end the war. After distancing itself from a statement by SCO in June last year condemning Israel's strikes, India has signed on to joint documents by the bloc censuring US-Israel military action against Iran.The Declaration reflected a major Indian concern as it strongly condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, emphasised that "double standards" in the fight against terrorism are unacceptable, and called on the international community to combat terrorism, including the cross-border movement of terrorists.It called for the UN playing a central role by fully implementing relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy in accordance with the UN Charter and the principles of international law to jointly combat all terrorist groups."Member States, reaffirming their firm commitment to combating terrorism, separatism, and extremism, emphasize the inadmissibility of attempts to exploit terrorist, separatist, and extremist groups for selfish purposes. They recognize the leading role of sovereign states and their competent authorities in countering terrorist and extremist threats," said the Declaration.Significantly, targeting use of economic sanctions by the West, the leaders came out in support of an open, fair and non-discriminatory multilateral trading system focused heavily on the framework established by the WTO, while slamming unilateral coercive measures."Member States oppose unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to the UN Charter and other norms of international law, the rules and principles of the World Trade Organization, that are detrimental to the interests of ensuring international security, including its food, energy and humanitarian components, and that have a negative impact on the global economy," said the Bishkek Declaration.
Article Summary: India joined other member-states in expressing condolences over the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei. This was the second time that the SCO denounced the strikes on Iran after the West Asia war started on February 28. India had endorsed that statement too, even though bilaterally it has not explicitly condemned the attacks on Iran.

Article Title: CJP’s proposed march on Sep 5 an attempt to create lawlessness before Brics: PIL in SC
Article Text:
“It is for the law enforcing agencies to ensure law and order while acting in accordance with law,” the CJI-led bench said

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to pass any interim orders on two PILs, including one by a retired police officer, seeking deferment of Cockroach Janata Party ‘s proposed march on Sep 5 by alleging that it is intended to create lawlessness ahead of Sep 12-13 BRICS summit in Delhi to deter participation of world leaders.When the petitioners questioned how such a march from the India Gate to the Police Headquarters can take place without permission, A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said there are two issues – one relates to law and order and the other to policy relating to permission to protest marches.“Let the stakeholders talk to them. As of now we have no reason to doubt that everyone would act and behave in a very responsible manner and in a peaceful and lawful manner. Right now, there is no compelling reason for us (the court) to presume that any wrong will happen. It is for the law enforcing agencies to ensure law and order while acting in accordance with law,” the CJI-led bench said.Appearing for one of the petitioners, advocate Syed Rizwan Ahmed said given the BRICS summit, till date no application seeking permission has been given to the authorities. In West Bengal, the previous govt did not give permission to so many protest rallies and the organizers had to move the HC for permission.Why does CJP, an unregistered entity not follow the same process? Are they above law, he asked.“God forbid another mishap, may not be by CJP, but by some mischievous elements take place, it will be covered by international media and deter participation of the foreign country leaders in BRICs,” he apprehended.The bench said, “All these factors are to be considered by some other quarters, not by us. There is nothing we can say right now. If something untoward or alarming happens, then file an application before us, provided the issue falls for determination in judicial domain.”The bench issued notice to the Centre on the two PILs, asked them to supply copies to the SC-constituted High-Powered Committee headed by retired SC judge R Subhash Reddy as well as the office of the solicitor general and posted these for hearing on Sep 10 along with petitions on July 20 incidents during protest march to Parliament, which turned violent resulting in alleged police excesses, injuries to protesters and security personnel and damage to public and private properties.When Ahmed asked whether CJP is above law and its processes, the bench said, “These are issues which are to be taken care of by the law and order enforcing agencies. It is their responsibility to maintain law and order. We expect both sides – protesters and law enforcing agencies - to respect, honour and follow the law of the land.”SC said it has referred a host of issues to the HPC, which is expected to give recommendations one after the other on them. When Ahmed persisted for a hearing on Sep 3 ahead of the proposed march, the bench said the petitioner must approach the Centre and Delhi police on the issue of absence of permission for the march. “Let them consider it,” it said.“There is no organized or identified group before us so that we can request them,” the bench said. Ahmed said that is another problem as CJP has no registered office where notice can be served. Can such an unorganized body hold the capital of the country to ransom, he asked.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court refused to pass any interim orders on two PILs, including one by a retired police officer. Cockroach Janata Party ‘s proposed march on Sep 5 by alleging that it is intended to create lawlessness ahead of Sep 12-13 BRICS summit in Delhi.

Article Title: BRICS Summit: Delhi Traffic Police issues advisory ahead of motorcade rehearsal
Article Text:

The rehearsal will be held between 10am and 3pm, with traffic regulations planned at 22 diversion points covering more than 35 roads. Article Title: CJP calls off Sept 5 march after SC quashes all FIRs against protesters on Centre's request
Article Text:
What were the three assurances

Why CJP had called for Sept 5 march
