NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party on Tuesday withdrew its call for a march on September 5 after Supreme Court , on the Centre's request, quashed all FIRs registered across the country against students who participated in the NEET protests."I want to state that in view of the positive assurances of the government of India and the judicial sanctity bestowed upon them today, and in view of the order being passed by this court, the CJP deems it appropriate to withdraw the call for the march on September 5 and looks forward to compliance with today's order," CJP co-convener Sourav Das said during a hearing in the Supreme Court.Chief Justice of India Surya Kant appreciated the CJP's decision, observing that disputes could be resolved if both sides acted in good faith."If both sides show good faith, then all issues can be resolved one by one. There is nothing in the world which is too complicated that it cannot be discussed with an open mind," the CJI said.This comes after Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre and Delhi Police, informed the apex court that the Centre remains committed to fulfilling all three assurances given to the leadership of CJP during the meeting between the Centre and the party.The first assurance was that the Centre would not pursue FIRs registered between July 20 and July 25.The second assurance was that no fresh FIRs would be registered in connection with the matter.The third assurance was that the government would pay compensation to students who died by suicide allegedly in connection with the NEET paper leak."Centre is committed to honour the assurance given to the CJP leaders to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide after NEET exam cancellation; however, 3 months needed to work out the modalities," Mehta told SC "As of now, we are committed to fulfilling all three assurances," he added.Earlier on Monday, Centre moved the apex court seeking to quash FIR's registered against the student protesters with alleged violence during protests over the NEET paper leak in Delhi and other states.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta mentioned the plea before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday, seeking the court’s intervention in the matter.The Centre has urged the Supreme Court to exercise its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to quash the FIRs registered against the protesting students.Also read: 'Keeping future of students in mind': Nadda after quashing of FIRs against NEET protesters. CJP had called for a protest march in Delhi on September 5, Teachers' Day. It had accused the Centre of failing to honour the promises made on July 25 to persuade the group to withdraw its 36-day agitation against irregularities in exams and the NEET paper leak.According to the CJP, the march was to be led by families of students who committed suicide following the cancellation of the NEET exam and the subsequent re-test, as well as those who were allegedly subjected to police excesses during the July agitation.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janata Party on Tuesday withdrew its call for a march on September 5. Supreme Court quashed all FIRs registered against students who participated in NEET protests. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant appreciated the CJP's decision, observing that disputes could be resolved if both sides acted in good faith.

Article Title: AIMPLB to launch campaign for protection Constitution and Sharia

The All India Muslim Personal Law Board will launch a movement on Sept 17

NEW DELHI: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board will launch a movement on Sept 17 to mobilise public opinion for protection of the Constitution and 'Sharia', religious freedom and rights and dignity of citizens. The Board plans to start the campaign from Jantar Mantar in Delhi and reach out to all faiths over three months.In a statement, the board said that as part of the campaign, a charter of demands will be submitted to the President of India Droupadi Murmu through governors in each state. Besides these issues, the charter will also include demands concerning elimination of hate crimes, prevention of unlawful demolitions, protection of Waqf properties and religious places, and equal enforcement of the law.The Board also proposes to bring out a ‘White Paper’ documenting incidents involving discrimination against Muslims, constitutional and human rights violations and release a comprehensive declaration on the issue of lynching.It said over the past several years conditions have emerged wherein vulnerable and marginalised sections, particularly Muslims, have been subjected to discriminatory treatment.The Board listed concerns ranging from extra-legal bulldozer demolitions, attempts to undermine Muslim Personal Law through Uniform Civil Code to undermining the beliefs of the minority community by making the singing of all six verses of Vande Mataram compulsory, as serious challenges to the Constitution of India, social harmony and national unity.Meanwhile, on the controversy following Kerala’s grand mufti Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad’s comments that women should remain confined to their homes and should not enter the public sphere, arguing that Islam prescribed the purdah system to protect their dignity, AIMPLB spokesperson SQR Ilyas objected to the remarks.Noting that Islam nowhere calls for women to be kept confined to the House for their safety, Ilyas said that the interpretation made by Ahmad is “not correct” and is therefore “misplaced.”He also cited the board’s profile highlighting that there were nearly 30 women in the AIMPLB and asserted that the board was fully in support of the idea of enabling Muslim women to progress which is in keeping with the Islamic teachings.

Article Title: SC: Why not use 'totaliser' to mix votes?
Article Text:
Supreme Court Tuesday sought Centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday sought Centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes from different EVMs before counting, to prevent any backlash from candidates by preserving voter anonymity.Petitioner advocate Ashwini Upadhyay said a totalisation system hides booth-wise voting patterns by mixing up votes from multiple electronic voting machines (typically around 14) before displaying the count, which helps protect voters from post-poll violence and political victimisation. Election Commission , through senior advocate D Seshadri Naidu, said the issue was referred by EC to govt, which consulted stakeholders and found it inadvisable to employ the 'totalisation' mechanism, mainly because of staunch opposition by political parties. He said a switch to this method would require changing the statute which the commission could not bring about.When Upadhyay pointed out that the totalisation mechanism was adopted by EC to count paper ballots, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked Centre to respond on why the same mechanism could not be adopted for EVMs. Upadhyay also said in Jan 2018, EC itself had told the court that the "time had come" to introduce the totaliser to "protect secrecy of the ballot and privacy of the individual".It had said that "the right of the people staying in a particular locality should not be exposed, and any kind of prejudice or discrimination because of the voting pattern should be avoided".In a U-turn, EC in its affidavit filed on Aug 31 said, "Experience of litigations has revealed that the present system which includes a simultaneous audit by the candidates is necessary to ensure that frivolous and baseless allegations do not cloud the outcome..." It said the introduction of the totaliser system would give fresh anxieties, misgivings and allegations regarding data, machine tampering and transmission glitches.
Article Summary: Supreme Court Tuesday sought Centre's response to the use of a 'totaliser' mechanism to mix votes from different EVMs before counting. Election Commission said the issue was referred by EC to govt, which consulted stakeholders and found it inadvisable to employ 'totalisation' mechanism.

Article Title: SC orders extradition of crypto accused
Article Text:
SC has directed Centre, CBI and Himachal govt to bring Subhash Sharma to justice by getting him extradited

NEW DELHI: Taking note that the main accused in Rs 20,000 crore cryptocurrency fraud case is safely holed up in Dubai for more than a year after duping around 2.5 lakh investors, SC has directed Centre, CBI and Himachal govt to bring Subhash Sharma to justice by getting him extradited. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran also directed attachment of all movable and immovable property of Sharma and his relatives.An FIR was registered in the case in 2023 and Sharma fled the country but the other accused were arrested in 2025.Granting bail to one of the accused in the case, the bench passed the order to extradite Sharma. It also requested Chief Justice of HP HC to constitute a special court to exclusively deal with this crime.
Article Summary: SC has directed Centre, CBI and Himachal govt to bring Subhash Sharma to justice by getting him extradited. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran also directed attachment of all movable and immovable property of Sharma and his relatives.

Article Title: NIA court orders attachment of accused’s property share in J&K terror-arms case
Article Text:
A special NIA court has ordered the attachment of the share of accused Fayaz Ahmed Mir in multiple properties in Kashmir

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

JAMMU: A special NIA court has ordered the attachment of the share of accused Fayaz Ahmed Mir in multiple properties in Kashmir while the trial in an alleged terror-linked arms case remains pending. Special Judge Prem Sagar passed the order Monday while allowing NIA’s application filed under Section 33(1) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, officials said.The properties listed in the order include 15 marlas (1 marla = 272.2sqft) of residential land, two shops spread over 2 marlas, and agricultural land measuring 25 marlas in Bumhama village of north Kashmir’s Baramulla district.The court directed that no third-party interest be created in the properties until the trial is over. The attachment applies only to Mir’s share in the listed properties and will remain in force until the proceedings conclude. A copy of the order has been forwarded to the Baramulla deputy commissioner for compliance, officials said.“Investigators alleged that Mir supplied arms, ammunition, and explosives to terrorists operating in south Kashmir, and received Rs 5.2 lakh in connection with an AK-47 rifle. The allegations are yet to be adjudicated by the trial court,” an official said.Mir’s counsel had opposed the attachment, arguing that the accused and his siblings had jointly inherited the properties, which were neither acquired through nor used for terrorist activities. The court, however, held that UAPA Section 33(1) permits attachment of property belonging to an accused facing trial for specified offences under the Act as a preventive measure.According to the case records, security forces intercepted a four-wheeler on the Srinagar-Jammu highway in Kulgam on Jan 11, 2020, and seized an AK-47 rifle, three pistols, a hand grenade and other incriminating materials. The occupants were identified as J&K Police DSP Devender Singh; Hizbul Mujahideen members Irfan Shafi Mir alias Advocate, Syed Naveed Mushtaq alias Naveed Babu and Rafi Ahmad Rather; former LoC trader Tanveer Ahmad Wani, and Naveed Babu’s brother Syed Irfan Ahmad. Four suspects, including two Hizbul terrorists, were arrested.
Article Summary: The properties listed in the order include 15 marlas (1 marla = 272.2sqft) of residential land, two shops spread over 2 marlas, and agricultural land measuring 25 marlas. Mir’s counsel had opposed the attachment, arguing that the accused and his siblings had jointly inherited the properties.

NEW DELHI: BJP has planned a trip of bikers between PM Narendra Modi’s birthplace Vadnagar in Gujarat and his parliamentary constituency Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh as part of its month-long events to celebrate his birthday on September 17, an exercise which will jibe with the party’s political campaign in the two states where assembly polls are due next year.With BJP looking to deepen its connect with the youth, Modi is expected to address students at Shri Ram College of Commerce to commemorate the institute's centenary celebrations on Sep 5.While BJP has been organising events every year to mark the leader’s birthday, it has scaled up the exercise this time as Modi will complete 25 years as head of govt, including as CM of Gujarat, on Oct 7.The events beginning on Sept 17, when Modi turns 76, will include drawing and speech contests for school students across the country, hackathon and innovation programme on social media and 25 welfare campaigns, sources said.A number of Union ministers and organisational functionaries, including Ashwini Vaishnaw, Mansukh Mandaviya, Smriti Irani, V D Sharma and Tejasvi Surya, have been roped in for various events.Party sources said 10 biker groups each from Vadnagar and Varanasi will travel between the two cities, and their trip will be marked by outreach to people along the way.While assembly polls are due early next year in UP, they will be held in Gujarat by end of next year.

LUCKNOW: Rivers in Uttar Pradesh reached or crossed danger levels at several monitoring stations as satellite data showed inundation of 11,358.49 hectares across five districts, highlighting the spread of flood conditions in the state. The affected districts are Ballia, Ghazipur, Gorakhpur, Mau and Deoria.The inundation figures were released by the Flood Management Information System Centre (FMISC) under the Uttar Pradesh irrigation department. Its satellite-based assessment, prepared using RISAT-1A MRS SAR data analysed by the National Remote Sensing Centre, showed major inundation in Ballia and Ghazipur and minor inundation in Gorakhpur, Mau and Deoria by Monday evening.Ballia reported flooding in 179 villages across 12 blocks, covering approximately 8,061.63 hectares. Ghazipur saw inundation in 87 villages across six blocks, covering 2,341.33 hectares. Deoria reported flooding in 18 villages across five blocks, Gorakhpur in 14 villages across three blocks, and Mau in 13 villages in one block.The combined assessment covered 311 villages in 27 blocks. The total submerged area was estimated at 11,358.49 hectares.The FMISC clarified that the assessment includes riverine flooding, water accumulation in low-lying areas, rainfall-induced flooding and isolated waterlogged patches.According to the Central Water Commission’s readings available at 9 pm on Tuesday, water levels were at or above the danger mark at 11 monitoring stations in Uttar Pradesh. The situation was serious along the Ganga, Ghaghra and their tributaries in Budaun, Barabanki, Ballia, Mirzapur, Varanasi and Ghazipur.At Kachhla Bridge in Budaun, the Ganga was flowing at 162.43 m, exactly at the danger level. Its warning level is 161.80 m.In Barabanki, the Ghaghra at Elginbridge was flowing at 106.09 m, 2 cm above its danger mark of 106.07 m and more than a metre above the warning level of 105.07 m. The CWC forecast suggested that the river could rise further to 106.07 m by 9 am on Wednesday.The Sharda also known as Mahakali river at Kukea in Lakhimpur Kheri rose to 139.81 m, marginally above its danger level of 139.8 m and well above the warning level of 138.8 m.The Ghaghra was also above the danger mark at Turtipar in Ballia, where it stood at 64.08 m against a danger level of 64.01 m. The station recorded 22 mm rainfall during the day. The forecast, however, indicated a fall to 64 m by Wednesday morning.In Ballia, the Ganga was flowing at 59.37 m, nearly 1.75 m above its danger level of 57.615 m. The district accounted for the largest share of the inundated area recorded by the state’s FMISC.The most pronounced river-level exceedances in eastern Uttar Pradesh were recorded along the Ganga and its tributaries. At Tendui in Varanasi district, the Varuna was flowing at 71.35 m against a danger level of 70.21 m. The station recorded 43 mm rainfall.At Saidpur in Ghazipur, the Ganga stood at 67.52 m against a danger level of 67.19 m. The station recorded 68 mm rainfall. At the Ghazipur monitoring station, the river was flowing at 63.33 m, exceeding the danger level of 63.105 m. The level was rising and was forecast to reach 63.47 m by 8 am on Wednesday. The station recorded 63 mm rainfall.In Mirzapur, the Ganga was above the danger mark at Ahraura and Chunar. At Ahraura, the river stood at 74.75 m against a danger level of 74.30 m, though the trend was declining. At Chunar, it was flowing at 72.82 m against a danger level of 72.78 m.At Narayanpur in Mirzapur, the Ganga was at 72.59 m, above the warning level of 71.41 metres but 21 cm below the danger mark of 72.41 m. The station recorded the highest rainfall among the locations shown in the CWC data, at 75.4 mm.The CWC data also recorded a high level at Chausa in neighbouring Bihar, where the Karamnasa was flowing at 61.86 m against a danger level of 60.39 m. The reading is significant for the downstream flood situation in eastern Uttar Pradesh.“The readings suggest that flood pressure is spread across multiple river systems rather than being confined to one stretch. While some stations showed a declining trend, water levels at several locations remained above danger marks, leaving riverbank settlements, agricultural fields, roads and embankments vulnerable,” said an official source.
Article Summary: Ballia, Ghazipur, Gorakhpur, Mau and Deoria are the worst affected districts. Water levels were at or above the danger mark at 11 monitoring stations in Uttar Pradesh. The situation was serious along the Ganga, Ghaghra and their tributaries.

NEW DELHI: The political row over the alleged purification ritual at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground following Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's rally last month has intensified, with the BJP Scheduled Caste Morcha performing a ‘buddhi-shuddhi’ ritual for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi at Panchayati Temple in Dehradun.The development came as Uttarakhand Congress chief Ganesh Godiyal led a massive protest march towards the state Secretariat, condemning the alleged ‘purification’ ritual conducted after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's August 8 rally in Haldwani.Accompanied by AICC co-in-charges Surendra Sharma and Manoj Yadav and hundreds of Congress workers, Godiyal attempted to gherao the Secretariat. Heavy police deployment was made to disperse the protesters, while several workers were detained as they raised slogans.The controversy centres on allegations that a ‘suddhikaran yajna’ was conducted at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground after Kharge's address. Congress leaders have criticised the alleged ritual, calling it an insult to the party president and an instance of caste discrimination."The rally happened in Haldwani, and then that place has a suddhikaran and havan. Then, the BJP State President justifies it and says that it is okay.What else could be more shameless?...BJP is working on the RSS agenda," Uttarakhand Assembly Leader of Opposition Yashpal Arya told ANI.The controversy also led to an FIR against Rahul Gandhi following a complaint by a member of the Scheduled Caste community, who alleged that the Congress leader's remarks about the purification ritual hurt the sentiments of the community.According to the complaint, members of the Valmiki community participated in cleaning the venue and conducting the ritual after the Congress rally attended by Kharge and other leaders.Godiyal, along with Surendra Sharma, Manoj Yadav and Congress workers, had also reached Dehradun's Kotwali Police Station on Monday seeking registration of an FIR against those responsible for the Haldwani incident.The row has since spread beyond Uttarakhand, with Congress units in several states protesting over the alleged ritual. Rahul Gandhi and AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi have also criticised the incident, describing it as a manifestation of a "Manuvadi mindset" and alleging that it was an attempt to demean a Dalit leader.The BJP has denied involvement in the ceremony. Union Minister and Leader of the House JP Nadda condemned the act in Parliament, saying the BJP had no association with the organisers and that the matter would be investigated.The organisers, Shri Ram Sena, along with local BJP representatives, maintained that the havan was not conducted because of Kharge's caste. They claimed the ritual was performed because religious decorum had allegedly been violated at the Ramlila Ground.
Article Summary: BJP Scheduled Caste Morcha performs 'buddhi-shuddhi' ritual for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi at Panchayati Temple in Dehradun. Uttarakhand Congress chief Ganesh Godiyal led a massive protest march towards the state Secretariat, condemning the alleged ‘purification’ ritual conducted after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's rally.

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress leader Abhishek Banerjee on Tuesday claimed that Bharatiya Janata Party-led West Bengal government was pursuing "political vendetta" against his party after he was questioned for nearly six hours by Kolkata Police over the removal of an unauthorised billboard.The Trinamool Congress MP from Diamond Harbour said that the Suvendu Adhikari-led government was selectively targeting TMC by removing its signboards, freezing party accounts and initiating cases against its leaders and workers."If they think they can silence us through false cases and arrests, they are mistaken," Abhishek Banerjee told reporters as he walked out of Shakespeare Sarani police station after questioning."They can question me but I am not scared, they are," he said, adding that the police action was a bid to weaken TMC.The TMC leader also alleged that several party workers arrested in connection with the incident were subjected to "custodial torture"."One of our workers, Tarik, was arrested and subjected to custodial torture. Police subsequently registered three FIRs and arrested several people.Abhishek, who has been named as an accused in two of the cases, was served a notice to appear before the police and arrived at the station around 12.15 pm, as TMC supporters gathered outside and raised slogans alleging that he was being targeted by the state government.The cases include sections pertaining to obstruction of government officials in the discharge of their duties, unlawful assembly, assault and harassment of women police personnel.

Article Title: Watch: CM Vijay steps out of convoy, gifts elderly woman his Dior glasses in Tamil Nadu
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: An unexpected roadside interaction between Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay and an elderly woman became one of the notable moments of his visit to Mettur in Salem district on Tuesday. During the brief encounter, Vijay gifted the woman his own pair of Christian Dior sunglasses.Vijay was in Salem to open the gates of the Mettur Dam and release water for Samba cultivation in the Cauvery Delta. News agency PTI reported that after inspecting the Mettur hydroelectric power station and opening the sluice gates of the Stanley Reservoir, he made an unscheduled stop at a roadside farm while travelling towards Salem airport.According to local accounts, Vijay noticed a group of elderly women working in the fields and stepped out of his vehicle to meet them.Chellam, an elderly resident of the area, walked towards the chief minister and held his hand.“He asked me if I had eaten,” Chellam recalled. “I told him I hadn't, because I was waiting to see him first.”During the interaction, Vijay asked her name and enquired about her well-being before walking with her around the garden and the nearby cattle shed belonging to local farmer Palanisamy.Chellam said the chief minister then offered her the sunglasses he was carrying.She later appeared in the oversized frames, walking beside Vijay with her hand on his arm and waving to people gathered along the route as he led her through the crowd.“I was surprised when he came and stood next to me. I told him how happy I was to see him, and he gifted me these sunglasses,” she told PTI.According to Chellam, Vijay’s gesture reminded her of his days in cinema.“He looked just like he does in his movies,” she said. “I was so happy I told him I would defend him if anyone ever tried to harm him.”The chief minister spent around 15 minutes at the farm, during which he distributed dhotis and sarees to the host family and discussed local agricultural issues, including the government’s decision to increase the milk procurement price to Rs 44.Chellam later said Vijay also urged her to have food. “He told me he had already eaten and insisted that I go and eat,” she said.Videos of the interaction were subsequently shared widely on social media. The visit also comes as the state government focuses on water release for Samba cultivation, with the Mettur Dam playing a key role in irrigation across the Cauvery Delta during the cropping season.
Article Summary: Vijay was in Salem to open the gates of the Mettur Dam and release water for Samba cultivation in the Cauvery Delta. He made an unscheduled stop at a roadside farm while travelling towards Salem airport. During the brief encounter, Vijay gifted the woman his own pair of Christian Dior sunglasses.

Article Title: The Rs 2.05 crore question: Can Meta be blamed for what its glasses record?
Article Text:
Secretly filmed by Meta glasses: Why a Delhi man is demanding Rs 2.05 crore (Reuters image)

So, what allegedly happened?

Why has Meta been named?

What Meta says about safeguards against covert recording

What studies have found about privacy and camera-equipped glasses

What the legal notice demands from Meta and the Instagram creator

A Delhi man has sent a legal notice to an Instagram creator and Meta Platforms after he was allegedly harassed and covertly filmed at a café using Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.The footage was subsequently posted on Instagram and viewed more than 4.19 lakh times.He has demanded that the video be removed, an apology issued and ₹2.05 crore paid in damages.But the notice, issued on August 24, goes beyond the actions of the creator. It seeks to hold Meta responsible in two capacities: as the owner of Instagram, which allegedly continued to host the reel after receiving complaints, and as the technology company behind the design and marketing of the camera-equipped glasses used to record it.The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF), which provided the victim pro bono legal assistance, says this is, to its knowledge, among the first legal actions in India to directly raise the liability of a smart-glasses maker for harm allegedly enabled by its product design.The case has not been decided by a court yet and the claims in the notice, so far, remain allegations. The man, whose identity has been withheld and who is referred to as X, is represented by advocate Apar Gupta.According to IFF, X was sitting alone at a Costa Coffee outlet in Delhi’s Khan Market on July 24 when a stranger, who eventually turned out to be a creator, approached him.The creator allegedly pestered and insulted him with unsolicited questions and remarks and followed him inside the café. X complained to the staff and eventually moved to another seating area to get away from the unpleasant situation thrust upon him.What he did not know, IFF says, was that the encounter was allegedly being recorded through Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses. One or more of the creator’s associates also allegedly filmed the exchange from other angles without his knowledge or consent.The footage was posted as an Instagram reel on July 26. By August 6, according to IFF, it had received more than 4.19 lakh views, approximately 15,700 likes and over 500 comments.X reported both the video and the account to Instagram on July 27. According to IFF, the reporting menu offered no category specifically covering invasion of privacy or non-consensual recording. The victim, therefore, selected “bullying or harassment”.He also submitted a separate complaint to Meta’s grievance officer for India under “Privacy violation — sharing of personal information or representation without consent.”Instagram subsequently informed him that the reported material doesn’t go against its “Community Standards”, according to IFF.The most significant part of the notice concerns the glasses themselves.Developed by Meta in partnership with eyewear company EssilorLuxottica, Ray-Ban Meta glasses resemble conventional eyewear but allow users to take photographs and record videos hands-free. They were launched in India in May 2025 at a starting price of ₹29,900.The glasses have a small white capture LED on the front that indicates when the camera is being used. The notice argues that this warning is inadequate because it can easily be missed by someone who does not know that the glasses contain a camera.“The recording indicator on the said devices is inadequate and easily overlooked, and the harm that eventuated to our client is due to a design that is foreseeably enabled,” the notice states.It argues that Meta “owed and breached a duty of care” to X and was negligent in contributing to the alleged intrusion into his privacy.Crucially, the notice argues that this liability arises from Meta’s own product-design and marketing decisions and is therefore separate from its role as an online intermediary.Section 79 of the Information Technology Act provides conditional protection to online intermediaries against liability for content posted by third parties. The notice contends that such protection cannot extend to a negligence claim arising from Meta’s own product design.That argument has not yet been tested in court.The Delhi dispute could now test a different question: whether a company that makes wearable cameras has a responsibility not merely to indicate that recording is taking place, but to ensure that an unsuspecting bystander can reasonably understand that they are being filmed.To know more, subscribe and read the full story on TOI+ — Secretly filmed by Meta glasses: Why a Delhi man is demanding Rs 2.05 crore
Article Summary: A Delhi man has sent a legal notice to an Instagram creator and Meta Platforms. He was allegedly harassed and covertly filmed at a café using Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses. The footage was subsequently posted on Instagram and viewed more than 4.19 lakh times. He has demanded that the video be removed, an apology issued and Rs 2.05 crore paid in damages.

Article Title: 'Can even become US president': Palaniswami takes dig at TN CM Vijay's 'PM ambitions'
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: As TVK leaders project Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay as the next Prime Minister, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami on Tuesday took a sharp jibe at TVK chief, saying that he could "even become the President of the United States."Mocking Vijay's extensive public relations campaigns and penchant for chartered flights, EPS said, "He could even become the President of America. There is nothing wrong with it, it is his wish.""They are running the government by putting out 'reels' here; that won't work there," he added.He also labelled Vijay as a "costly chief minister" and contrasted the current administration's expenditure with that of former chief minister J Jayalalithaa."During Amma's tenure, projects were inaugurated via video conferencing to cut costs," Palaniswami said.This comes amid a recent push by TVK leaders to project Vijay as a potential contender for the PM's post. TVK PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna had earlier said the country's top constitutional office should be held by a leader from Tamil Nadu.TVK leaders, including KA Sengottaiyan and D Sarathkumar, have compared Vijay with former Tamil Nadu chief ministers MGR and Jayalalithaa, claiming he would not only rule Tamil Nadu but also lead the country in the future.TVK MLA Kallanai, who organised an event marking the party's 100 days in office, said people had immense faith in Vijay's leadership. He expressed confidence that Vijay would eventually lead the country and hoist the national flag at the Red Fort as a representative of the Tamil people, news agency PTI reported.Congress MP Karti Chidambaram said that while party workers may have deep admiration for their leader, national leadership ultimately depends on securing the numbers required to form a government."I fully accept that they have great love, affection, expectation, and admiration for their party leadership. This is their party. What they say within their party makes no difference to the public discourse. In public discourse, what you should ask about is policy and the law. Their wishes within a party make no difference to me," Chidambaram told reporters, according to ANI.He said every political party has its own ambitions and aspirations, but any prime ministerial aspirant must ultimately have the numbers to command a majority in Lok Sabha."Every party has dreams, ambitions, and desires. One cannot pass laws to stop that. Everyone expresses their own wishes and talks about their favourite leader in their party. But we know what the political reality is. There are 543 constituencies," Chidambaram said.The issue has gained further attention after a private media survey placed Vijay among the preferred candidates for PM in 2029, behind PM Narendra Modi and Rahul Gandhi.The TVK government was formed after the 2026 Tamil Nadu assembly elections, when the party emerged as the largest force and formed the government with support from VCK, IUML, Congress, CPI and CPM.
Article Summary: TVK leaders project Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay as the next Prime Minister. AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami takes a sharp jibe at TVK chief, saying he could "even become the President of the United States"
